UPON INSPECTION THE CAN WAS FOUND TO HAVE A MOUNTING BRACKET BROKEN OFF OF IT. THE BREAK WAS WHERE THE BRACKET WAS WELDED TO THE CAN AND IT ACTUALLY WAS THE CAN ITSELF THAT HAD BROKEN, NOT THE BRACKET. THE OPPOSITE ENGINE WAS INSPECTED AND IT HAD A SIMILAR CRACK. IN RESEARCHING THIS PART, IT WAS FOUND THAT IN THE PAST YEAR, THIS PART HAD BEEN REPLACED ON 6 OTHER ENGINES FOR THE SAME REASON AT THIS LOCATION. THIS DEFINITELY SEEMS TO BE AN ITEM THAT DESERVES MORE ATTENTION WHEN INSPECTING THE ENGINES.

During cruise of the flight from SWF to IAD, the crew reported that the L/H engine had flamed out.  The engine oil pressure had been normal and there were no abnormal engine indications prior to the flame-out.  The aircraft was diverted to ABE where it was landed without incident.  Maintenance personnel found the splined shaft between the fuel control and fuel pump had sheared.  The fuel control and fuel pump were removed and replaced.  Operational and leak checks were satisfactory and the aircraft was returned to service.

ON THE RAMP, THE PILOT REPORTED FUEL LEAKING FROM THE INBOARD NR 1 ENGINE DRAIN LINE.  MAINTENANCE DISCOVERED THE LOW PRESSURE FUEL PUMP WAS REPLACED.  DISASSEMBLY OF THE PUMP REVEALED THAT THE DIAPHRAGM IN THE PRESSURE ADJUSTING VALVE HAD A HOLE IN IT.  FURTHER INSPECTION DETERMINED THAT THE PN RA531 DIAPHRAGM CONTROL PLATE, THAT CONTACTS THE DIAPHRAGM, DID NOT CONFORM TO THE LEAR SIEGLER/ ROMEC PLATE DESIGN DRAWING FOR FINAL FINISH OF THE OUTER CIRCUMFERENCE OF THE PLATE.  SHARP EDGES THAT REMAIN ON THIS PLATE HAVE THE CAPACITY TO CAUSE A HIGH RATE OF WEAR ON THE RUBBER DIAPHRAGM, CAUSING EARLY FAILURE OF THE DIAPHRAGM AND RESULTING IN FUEL LEAKAGE.

WHILE INFLIGHT FROM PANAMA CITY, FLORIDA THE LEFT ENGINE LOW OIL PRESSURE ANNUNCIATOR ILLUMINATED.  THE OIL PRESSURE WAS BELOW 60 PSI.  THE ENGINE WAS SHUT DOWN AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS RETURNED TO FIELD WITH NO FURTHER INCIDENT.  THE CORRECTIVE ACTION WAS THE THE LEFT GAS GENERATOR AND THE POWER SECTION WAS REPLACED.  THE TEARDOWN REPORT REVEALED THAT THE PROPELLER SHAFT HAS SEIZED AND THERE WAS NO OIL INDICATION ON THE DIPSTICK.  THE CAUSE OF THE OVERHEATING DISTRESS TO THE PLANET GEAR `Y` OCCURRED FROM LACK OF LUBRICATION.

AFTER LANDING IN NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA ON FLIGHT 5518, THE LEFT ENGINE WENT INTO REVERSE. THE ENGINE WAS DETERMINED TO BE IN BETA AND LIMITS WERE NOT EXCEEDED PER PRATT & WHITNEY MANUAL.  THEREFORE NO PARTS WERE USED.

During Cruise on Flt 256 EWR - PUJ, the Flight Attendant reported a spark coming out of aft center oven. Flt crew turned oven of and pulled circuit breaker immediatley. On ground at PUJ, Maintenance performed an operational check I/A/W AMM 25-35-00-501 with no defects noted. DURING CAT2 AUTOLAND, AT APPROX 20-30 FT, AIRCRAFT PITCHED UP AUTOMATICALLY, THEN AT 15 FT AUTOPILOT DISCONNECTED ITSELF. CAPTAIN TOOK OVER AND MANUALLY LANDED.  THERE WAS A FAILURE OF THE RT AUTOPILOT RUDDER SERVO ON THIS AIRPLANE DURING A PREVIOUS FLT. AS A RESULT,  THE RT RUDDER SERVO CIRCUIT BREAKER WAS PULLED AND COLLARED AND THE AC WAS IN A CAT2 STATUS WHEN THIS EVENT OCCURRED. THE MCDP REPORTED THE AUTOPILOT DISCONNECT WAS CAUSED BY A PITCH AXIS MODE ERROR.  THIS EITHER CAN BE CAUSED BY THE PILOT OVERRIDING THE PITCH SERVO, OR THE ELEVATOR SURFACE POSITION DIFFERING FROM THE ELEVATOR SERVO POSITION BY MORE THAN FOUR DEGREES.  THE RT RUDDER SERVO AND RT FCC WERE REPLACED AND THE AC WAS RESTORED TO CAT3.

THERE IS AN EXHAUST ELBOW THAT COMES OFF THE WASTEGATE AND RETURNS TO THE TAILPIPE.  THIS PIPE HAD WORN NEARLY THROUGH AT THE SLIP JOINT BETWEEN IT AND THE TAIL PIPE.  THE TAIL PIPE WAS WORN TO A SHARP EDGE WHERE THE ELBOW ENTERS THE SLIP JOINT.  THIS CONDITION WAS NOT VISIBLE UNTIL THE TAILPIPE WAS REMOVED.  PROBABLE CAUSE IT THE VIBRATION BETWEEN THE TWO PIPES.  THE TAILPIPE NEEDS TO BE REMOVED EVERY 200 HOURS TO INSPECT THIS JOINT FOR DAMAGE.  UNDETECTED, THIS EXHAUST PIPE WOULD HAVE FAILED IN A FEW MORE HOURS.  THIS FAILURE COULD HAVE CAUSED AN INFLIGHT FIRE AND POSSIBLE LOSS OF LIFE.
